name: WritingBench
ability_definition: The ability to communicate information and ideas in writing so others will understand.

task_realism.reasoning: Queries span 6 domains and 100 subdomains of practical writing: academic and engineering reports, business and finance documents, legal and political texts, educational materials, and marketing copy. Many include reference materials and explicit requirements, much like real workplace writing requests. However, the queries are partly LLM-generated and then human-refined, not drawn from actual workplace assignments, so some are stylized or idealized.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Testing is single-shot generation from a self-contained prompt. There is no iterative drafting, stakeholder feedback, information gathering, organizational context, or consequence for miscommunication. An LLM critic does the grading, not an actual intended reader. The dynamic criteria reportedly reach about 87% agreement with humans, but conditions remain far from real work, where writing is revised, contextualized and judged by recipients.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Genre breadth is strong. Query-specific criteria cover clarity, organization, audience fit, style, format and length, which are core parts of communicating in writing. The benchmark does not directly measure whether readers actually understand the content or can act on it, which is the essence of the O*NET definition. It also underweights short everyday workplace writing such as emails and quick explanations, and it omits multi-turn and collaborative writing.

format_match.reasoning: Outputs are free-form, full-length documents in real genres, with genuine format and length constraints, which makes them close to real work artifacts. Inputs are natural-language requests, sometimes with source material. The only departures from authentic workplace artifacts are the lack of real templates, attachments, and organizational conventions.

transferability_reasoning: WritingBench offers broad, realistic writing tasks with authentic document-style outputs and task-specific criteria that track human judgment reasonably well, so it transfers moderately well to Written Expression. Transfer is limited by single-shot, context-free conditions and by LLM-judged rubric compliance standing in for actual reader comprehension. Performance should indicate real writing competence across genres but may overstate effectiveness in real, iterative, audience-specific workplace communication.

2025.metric: WritingBench overall score on a 0-100 scale (the 1-10 judge score multiplied by 10)
2025.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated professionals who write as part of their jobs, such as reports, business documents, marketing copy, educational material and legal or policy drafts. They are not specialist professional writers or domain experts working only in their own field.

2026.metric: WritingBench overall score: mean of 5 per-task criteria on a 1–10 scale, multiplied by 10 to give a 0–100 scale (reported as a 0.839 fraction)
2026.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical college-educated professionals who write documents such as reports, business and legal documents, marketing copy, educational materials and academic text as part of their work.
